steps.text: A Stepanov-type determinant.
Vanishing of D^p on a CM curve when p is inert, and a divisibility bound with an O(log a) error.
Rewriting q^N = M^k + R with a quadric form, aiming at automorphy through a theta-series period on a sixfold cover of GL5.
W(1_S) ≥ 0 via a determinant, read as Stepanov's method at multiplicity one; a bootstrap.
A weighted von Mangoldt sum, a Guinand–Weil sign and a variance trick; Bertini gives a sign, iterated Parseval gives square-root cancellation.
W applied to combinations of indicator functions, for a lower bound above 1 − η.
Determinants of W-functions containing GGP periods, taking values 0 or 1 (interlacing).
Iterated theta lifts between totally definite unitary groups, each adding a Hecke twist; about √X lifts give multiplicity m.
Norm and level estimates for the lifts using Chowla–Selberg, Weyl and the Siegel mass formula.
A lower bound on the divisibility of the m-fold iterated lift.
An Iwasawa tower, by analogy with pigeonhole over F_{q^n}/F_q.
Seesaw: the period of the iterated lift is a Bessel period independent of the Hecke characters (Rallis).
The Bost slope inequality.
The cost of each lift; a priori stopping point 2/3, needing a main term and a division step.
Gluing an integral structure across Hecke characters, a gcd-like average.
A relative trace formula; Cauchy–Schwarz reduces to a norm bound on a projected Poincaré series.
Galois cohomology classes in H¹ that twisting cannot kill: a weak form of Vandiver's conjecture.
Covolumes, the index of theta series, and congruences between lifts and forms.
The choice of Iwasawa tower, with a Behrend-type trick.
GRH.

summaries.8: The whole proof in one statement: for every Dirichlet character χ, L(χ, s) ≠ 0 whenever Re(s) > ½ (leaving out the pole of ζ at s = 1). RH and GRH follow from this.
summaries.10: Mathlib's Riemann Hypothesis, obtained from the statement for every character by taking the trivial character.
summaries.21: Turns 'no zeros right of ½ for every character' into Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis.
summaries.20: Turns the same statement into 'zeros of a primitive L-function in the critical strip lie on Re(s) = ½', using the functional equation.
summaries.16: The central claim: L(χ, s) ≠ 0 for every Dirichlet character χ and every s with Re(s) > ½ (except ζ at s = 1).
summaries.17: Proves the central claim by feeding the Galois-representation statement (Row0b) into the main argument.
summaries.23: Reduces the central claim to Row0b: attaching ℓ-adic Galois representations with prescribed properties to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representations over CM fields.
summaries.42: Derives the central claim from a bundle of literature statements (local Langlands existence, Galois representations of polarized pairs) together with VWin, a bound for every character.
summaries.152: The analytic core, by size: the central claim follows from hypotheses on unitary groups at a third place, local theta inputs, agreement of theta integrals, local matching, a covolume bound, local Langlands existence and VWin.
summaries.596: Shows that the family of objects needed on the definite side can actually be built from those inputs. About a third of the whole proof sits under this one result.
summaries.2035: Builds the required objects from unramified exponents for unitary groups.
summaries.1778: From the unitary-group hypotheses, proves a surjectivity statement and a lower bound for a quantity Λ.
summaries.1767: Proves an open-orbit statement for the parameters from the unitary-group hypotheses.
summaries.462: Closes the argument from a 'Green' condition, VWin and the non-emptiness of the definite-side hypotheses.
summaries.126: A covolume bound from arithmetic geometry: resolution and principalisation in characteristic 0, Moriwaki bigness, Fargues, Zarhin and nef Riemann–Roch statements.
summaries.398: Packages the Arakelov-geometry inputs into the statement used for the volume bound.
summaries.6454: Existence of a good tower together with a volume theorem, from arithmetic intersection theory.
summaries.461: The covolume bound used in the core, from volume estimates, Hodge bundle theorems and Grothendieck deformation theory.
summaries.41: Proves VWin, the bound for every character, from the Galois-representation statement Row0b.
summaries.144: VWin from an open-image condition, isobaric base change and a Galois input.
summaries.1953: VWin from an automorphy statement in rank n.
summaries.22: Proves Row0b: Galois representations with the required local–global compatibility, with local parameters given by local Langlands.
summaries.40: Constructs those Galois representations by way of theta lifts.
summaries.143: Geometric realization in weight one, a step in building the Galois representations.
summaries.511: Geometric realization in weight one, from a holomorphic Lefschetz formula.
summaries.1922: A Kodaira–Spencer statement in weight one.
